title: One generic Engine executes both domains without domain-specific runtime branches
claim: The EOO Engine can perform reads, Functions, governed Actions, authority/policy checks, durable execution, observations and provenance for Manufacturing and Project Ontology using generic resource/capability dispatch only.
null_hypothesis: The shared Engine is superficial; each domain needs hidden special-case branches or bespoke orchestration to execute correctly.
rivals: A plugin framework with per-domain handlers is the real architecture and should be acknowledged instead of calling the Engine generic.
Generic execution works only because the two domains are too similar.
mechanism: If operational semantics live in typed resource definitions, contracts and adapters, the Engine should interpret capabilities generically while domain-specific external integrations remain behind declared adapters.
scope: All registered read/function/action/governance paths in Manufacturing and Project Ontology.
predictions: Core Engine contains zero branches keyed to domain id or named domain object/action types.
Both domains traverse the same action lifecycle states and provenance model.
Domain adapters implement external binding only, not generic governance semantics.
A generated synthetic object/action using existing resource kinds can execute without editing Engine core.
falsifiers: A required domain behavior can only be implemented by editing Engine core with a domain-specific branch.
A domain adapter performs authority/policy/governance semantics that the Engine claims to own.
A new ordinary action type requires Engine code changes rather than configuration/adapter code.

experiment.summary: Instrument and audit Engine dispatch while executing full suites for both domains and generated synthetic resources.
steps: Freeze allowed Engine extension points and forbidden domain-identity dependencies.
Run both domain suites with branch/handler tracing.
Static-scan Engine core for domain names and registered domain object/action identifiers.
Generate synthetic definitions using existing resource kinds and execute them.
Inject a domain-name branch and governance-in-adapter mutation.

oracle: Frozen generic execution state machine and allowlist of adapter responsibilities.
baseline: Explicit plugin architecture with per-domain handlers, measured honestly as a simpler rival.

support_if: 100% registered domain operations use generic lifecycle states.
0 governance semantics found in adapters beyond declared external binding responsibilities.
Generated synthetic resource/action executes without Engine edit.
reject_if: Any required domain-specific Engine branch or undeclared governance-in-adapter behavior is necessary.
inconclusive_if: Either domain does not exercise at least read, Function, governed Action, security and provenance paths.
invalid_if: Static audit excludes files that actually participate in Engine semantic dispatch.

python_hypothesis_role.strategy: Generate valid generic resources/actions and operation sequences; use instrumentation to assert generic dispatch invariants.
python_hypothesis_role.mutation_proof: Insert `if domain_id == ...` behavior and move a policy check into an adapter; audits/tests must fail.

stop_conditions: If domain-specific Engine branching is required, expose it as plugin architecture and reject the stronger generic-Engine claim.
